accepted.s: PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan is best described as a:
accepted.x: PM Gati Shakti is a whole-of-government, GIS-based integrated planning initiative for infrastructure development.
accepted.tq: Use the precise institutional description rather than a related infrastructure objective.
accepted.sec: PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan - launch, engines, ministries, platform  [APPSC]

accepted.s: On which date was the PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan launched?
accepted.x: The PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan was launched on 13 October 2021.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between closely associated launch dates.
accepted.sec: PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan - launch, engines, ministries, platform  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the institutional structure of PM Gati Shakti:
1. The Empowered Group of Secretaries is headed by the Cabinet Secretary.
2. The Network Planning Group functions within the structure.
3. A Technical Support Unit is included in the structure.
4. The structure has been replicated in the States.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements correctly describe the institutional structure and its replication in the States.
accepted.tq: When all components are expressly listed, test the complete combination.
accepted.sec: PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan - launch, engines, ministries, platform  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the evolution of ministry participation and the current EGoS coverage under PM Gati Shakti?
o: 23 ministries were initially brought on one platform, while 16 are now on the EGoS
16 ministries were initially brought on one digital platform, while 23 infrastructure and user ministries are now on the EGoS
16 ministries were initially brought on one platform, while 30 are now on the EGoS
Seven ministries were initially brought on one platform, while 16 are now on the EGoS
accepted.x: The platform initially brought together 16 ministries; the EGoS now covers 23 infrastructure and user ministries.
accepted.tq: Separate the initial figure from the later expanded figure.
accepted.sec: PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan - launch, engines, ministries, platform  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The NMP portal of PM Gati Shakti was developed by:
accepted.x: The portal, containing more than 1,700 data layers, was developed by BISAG-N of Gandhinagar.
accepted.tq: Apply the organisation-location association carefully.
accepted.sec: PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan - launch, engines, ministries, platform  [APPSC]

accepted.s: How many railway economic corridor projects, involving what approximate investment, were mapped on the PM Gati Shakti portal?
accepted.x: The portal mapped 434 railway economic corridor projects with an investment of ₹11.17 lakh crore.
accepted.tq: Match the project count with its corresponding investment figure.
accepted.sec: PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan - launch, engines, ministries, platform  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The National Infrastructure Pipeline covered which period?
accepted.x: The National Infrastructure Pipeline covered the period from FY2019-20 to FY2024-25.
accepted.tq: Use the exact beginning and ending financial years.
accepted.sec: National Infrastructure Pipeline - period, investment, sectors, coverage, split  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The original investment size associated with the National Infrastructure Pipeline was approximately:
accepted.x: The National Infrastructure Pipeline was originally associated with an investment of approximately ₹111 lakh crore.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the original NIP estimate from NMP values and later pipeline estimates.
accepted.sec: National Infrastructure Pipeline - period, investment, sectors, coverage, split  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the coverage of the National Infrastructure Pipeline?
o: It covers both economic and social infrastructure.
accepted.x: The NIP covers both economic and social infrastructure, rather than being restricted to economic infrastructure.
accepted.tq: Reject the restrictive word ‘only’ when the broader coverage is correct.
accepted.sec: National Infrastructure Pipeline - period, investment, sectors, coverage, split  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following sectors of the National Infrastructure Pipeline in descending order of their approximate shares:
A. Railways
B. Energy
C. Urban infrastructure
D. Roads
accepted.x: The approximate shares are energy 24%, roads 18%, urban infrastructure 17% and railways 12%.
accepted.tq: Order the options by comparing the numerical shares from highest to lowest.
accepted.sec: National Infrastructure Pipeline - period, investment, sectors, coverage, split  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly represents the approximate funding split of the National Infrastructure Pipeline?
accepted.x: The funding split was approximately Centre 39%, States 40% and private sector 21%.
accepted.tq: Match each percentage with the correct funding source rather than merely recalling the figures.
accepted.sec: National Infrastructure Pipeline - period, investment, sectors, coverage, split  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The National Infrastructure Pipeline has subsequently been described as a pipeline of approximately ₹185–213 lakh crore across:
o: 30 or more sectors, including digital and social infrastructure
50 or more sectors, restricted to transport
accepted.x: The expanded description refers to ₹185–213 lakh crore across more than 30 sectors, including digital and social infrastructure.
accepted.tq: Link the range of investment to the correct sectoral coverage.
accepted.sec: National Infrastructure Pipeline - period, investment, sectors, coverage, split  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following is a correct feature of the National Monetisation Pipeline?
o: It concerns agricultural land whose ownership is transferred to States.
It concerns brownfield core infrastructure assets while ownership remains with the Government.
It concerns only greenfield private assets whose ownership is permanently transferred.
It concerns only newly constructed airports owned by private companies.
accepted.x: The NMP monetises brownfield core infrastructure assets through appropriate instruments while ownership remains with the Government.
accepted.tq: Identify the option that combines the asset type with the ownership principle.
accepted.sec: National Monetisation Pipeline - period, value, largest sector, assets  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The National Monetisation Pipeline was announced in the:
accepted.x: The National Monetisation Pipeline was announced in the Union Budget 2021-22.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the announcement year from later implementation and revision years.
accepted.sec: National Monetisation Pipeline - period, value, largest sector, assets  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly matches NMP 1.0 with its period and value?
accepted.x: NMP 1.0 covered FY22-FY25 and had a value of ₹6 lakh crore.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure period-value pair and eliminate mismatched combinations.
accepted.sec: National Monetisation Pipeline - period, value, largest sector, assets  [APPSC]

accepted.s: In NMP 1.0, which sector was the largest sector?
accepted.x: Roads were the largest sector under NMP 1.0.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the largest sector in NMP 1.0 from the sectoral distribution in NMP 2.0.
accepted.sec: National Monetisation Pipeline - period, value, largest sector, assets  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about NMP 1.0:
1. It envisaged a value of ₹6 lakh crore.
2. Approximately ₹5.3 lakh crore was monetised.
3. Coal contributed the largest amount, approximately ₹2 lakh crore.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: NMP 1.0 was valued at ₹6 lakh crore; about ₹5.3 lakh crore, or roughly 89–90%, was monetised, with coal contributing about ₹2 lakh crore.
accepted.tq: Check each numerical statement against the complete NMP 1.0 outcome.
accepted.sec: National Monetisation Pipeline - period, value, largest sector, assets  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which statement correctly describes NMP 2.0?
o: It covers FY25-FY27 and is valued at ₹10 lakh crore only.
It covers FY22-FY25 and is valued at ₹6 lakh crore.
It covers FY26-FY30 and excludes private participation.
It covers FY26-FY30 and is valued at ₹16.72 lakh crore, including ₹5.8 lakh crore from private participation.
accepted.x: NMP 2.0 covers FY26-FY30 and has a value of ₹16.72 lakh crore, including ₹5.8 lakh crore of private participation.
accepted.tq: Separate the period, total value and private component of the second pipeline.
accepted.sec: National Monetisation Pipeline - period, value, largest sector, assets  [APPSC]

accepted.s: NMP 2.0 was launched on:
accepted.x: NMP 2.0 was launched on 23 February 2026 and was prepared by NITI Aayog.
accepted.tq: Use the exact launch date rather than the date of the first NMP.
accepted.sec: National Monetisation Pipeline - period, value, largest sector, assets  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following represents the correct descending order of the major NMP 2.0 sectoral shares?
o: Railways and ports, power, coal, highways/MMLPs/ropeways
Highways/MMLPs/ropeways, power, railways and ports, coal
Coal, railways and ports, power, highways/MMLPs/ropeways
Power, highways/MMLPs/ropeways, coal, railways and ports
accepted.x: The shares are highways/MMLPs/ropeways 26%, power 17%, railways 16%, ports 16% and coal 13%.
accepted.tq: Arrange the listed sectors by their stated percentages and notice the tied railway-port share.
accepted.sec: National Monetisation Pipeline - period, value, largest sector, assets  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT an instrument of asset monetisation under the NMP?
o: Direct cancellation of all public ownership
accepted.x: The listed instruments include PPP concessions, InvITs, Toll-Operate-Transfer and securitisation. Direct cancellation of public ownership is not an NMP instrument.
accepted.tq: Identify the option that changes ownership rather than describing a monetisation instrument.
accepted.sec: National Monetisation Pipeline - period, value, largest sector, assets  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The NMP is monitored by the:
o: Securities and Exchange Board of India
accepted.x: The NMP is monitored by the Cabinet Group on Asset Monetisation, or CGAM, headed by the Cabinet Secretary.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the monitoring body from the planning and regulatory bodies.
accepted.sec: National Monetisation Pipeline - period, value, largest sector, assets  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Bharatmala Pariyojana is primarily associated with:
accepted.x: Bharatmala Pariyojana is a road-sector programme focused on national highway corridors and related connectivity.
accepted.tq: Separate the road-sector programme from the port-sector programme Sagarmala.
accepted.sec: Bharatmala and Sagarmala - sector, phases, components, objectives  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Phase I of Bharatmala Pariyojana:
1. It was launched in 2017.
2. It covers 34,800 km of National Highway corridors.
3. Its coverage extends to more than 580 districts.
4. It includes economic corridors, inter-corridors, feeder routes, border connectivity and port connectivity.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements correctly describe Bharatmala Phase I, including its 2017 launch, scale, district coverage and corridor components.
accepted.tq: Test the programme through its date, scale, geographical reach and components.
accepted.sec: Bharatmala and Sagarmala - sector, phases, components, objectives  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Multi-Modal Logistics Parks are associated in the material with:
accepted.x: Multi-Modal Logistics Parks form a component associated with Bharatmala Pariyojana.
accepted.tq: Match the component with the programme to which it belongs.
accepted.sec: Bharatmala and Sagarmala - sector, phases, components, objectives  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Sagarmala is an initiative based on:
accepted.x: Sagarmala is based on port-led development and was included in the National Perspective Plan of 2016.
accepted.tq: Use the defining objective to distinguish Sagarmala from Bharatmala.
accepted.sec: Bharatmala and Sagarmala - sector, phases, components, objectives  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT a pillar of Sagarmala?
accepted.x: Sagarmala's pillars include port modernisation, port connectivity, port-led industrialisation, coastal community development, and coastal shipping and inland water transport.
accepted.tq: Find the option outside the programme's stated pillars.
accepted.sec: Bharatmala and Sagarmala - sector, phases, components, objectives  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes Sagarmala's scale and recent development?
o: 434 projects involving ₹11.17 lakh crore; Sagarmala 2.0 was introduced in 2021
800-plus projects involving about ₹5.8 lakh crore; Sagarmala 2.0 was introduced in 2025
34,800 projects involving ₹5.8 lakh crore; Sagarmala 2.0 was introduced in 2017
800-plus projects involving ₹16.72 lakh crore; Sagarmala 2.0 was introduced in 2026
accepted.x: Sagarmala comprises more than 800 projects involving about ₹5.8 lakh crore, and Sagarmala 2.0 was introduced in 2025.
accepted.tq: Combine the project scale, investment and revision year without swapping them with other programmes.
accepted.sec: Bharatmala and Sagarmala - sector, phases, components, objectives  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Coastal shipping under Sagarmala increased by approximately what percentage over a decade?
accepted.x: Coastal shipping increased by approximately 118% over the decade referred to.
accepted.tq: Discriminate among close percentage values.
accepted.sec: Bharatmala and Sagarmala - sector, phases, components, objectives  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The share of railway routes electrified increased from 50.91% in March 2019 to approximately what share of broad-gauge routes by October 2025?
accepted.x: Electrification rose from 50.91% of routes in March 2019 to 99.1% of broad-gauge routes by October 2025.
accepted.tq: Match the later percentage with the correct earlier base figure.
accepted.sec: Railway infrastructure - electrification, National Rail Plan, net zero  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The National Rail Plan 2030 aims to raise the railways' freight share from:
accepted.x: The National Rail Plan 2030 aims to increase the railways' freight share from 28% to 45%.
accepted.tq: Preserve the direction of change while distinguishing the two percentage points.
accepted.sec: Railway infrastructure - electrification, National Rail Plan, net zero  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which pair of objectives is associated with the National Rail Plan 2030?
o: Raise rail freight share to 45% and expand Kavach
Maintain rail freight share at 28% and expand only waterways
Reduce rail freight share to 28% and discontinue Kavach
Raise rail freight share to 60% and privatise all routes
accepted.x: The National Rail Plan 2030 seeks to raise rail's freight share from 28% to 45% and expand Kavach.
accepted.tq: Select the option containing both stated objectives without an exaggerated claim.
accepted.sec: Railway infrastructure - electrification, National Rail Plan, net zero  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Indian Railways has set the target of achieving net-zero emissions by:
accepted.x: The target for Indian Railways is net-zero emissions by 2030.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the target year from nearby infrastructure milestones.
accepted.sec: Railway infrastructure - electrification, National Rail Plan, net zero  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following statements about the Dedicated Freight Corridors is correct?
o: 1,337 km of the 2,843 km network had been completed by October 2025.
2,843 km of the 2,741 km network had been completed by October 2025.
4,343 km of the 2,843 km network had been completed by October 2025.
2,741 km of the 2,843 km network had been completed by October 2025.
accepted.x: By October 2025, 2,741 km out of 2,843 km had been completed, equivalent to about 96.4%.
accepted.tq: Check numerator and denominator before accepting the completion percentage.
accepted.sec: Railway infrastructure - electrification, National Rail Plan, net zero  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Eastern DFC — 1,337 km; Western DFC — JICA
Eastern DFC — JICA; Western DFC — World Bank
Eastern DFC — 2,843 km; Western DFC — World Bank
Eastern DFC — 1,337 km; Western DFC — NITI Aayog
accepted.x: The Eastern Dedicated Freight Corridor is associated with 1,337 km and the World Bank, while the Western DFC is associated with JICA.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure institutional pair and verify the corridor detail.
accepted.sec: Railway infrastructure - electrification, National Rail Plan, net zero  [APPSC]

accepted.s: As of March 2025, the railway network had approximately:
accepted.x: The railway network measured 69,439 route kilometres as of March 2025.
accepted.tq: Distinguish network length from corridor length and electrification percentage.
accepted.sec: Railway infrastructure - electrification, National Rail Plan, net zero  [APPSC]

accepted.s: South Coast Railway, headquartered at Visakhapatnam, became operational on:
accepted.x: South Coast Railway, with headquarters at Visakhapatnam, became operational on 1 June 2026.
accepted.tq: Separate the railway operational date from the airport inauguration and operations dates.
accepted.sec: Railway infrastructure - electrification, National Rail Plan, net zero  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The National Investment and Infrastructure Fund is correctly described as a:
o: Statutory bank created under the NaBFID Act, 2021
SEBI-regulated trust created in 2014 to pool operating infrastructure
Government-anchored quasi-sovereign wealth fund managing Category II Alternative Investment Funds, set up in 2015
Non-Banking Financial Company established in 2006 for PPP finance
accepted.x: NIIF is government-anchored, manages Category II AIFs, functions as a quasi-sovereign wealth fund and was set up in 2015.
accepted.tq: Distinguish NIIF from NaBFID, IIFCL and InvITs by its institutional character.
accepted.sec: Infrastructure financing and PPP - NIIF, NaBFID, IIFCL, InvITs, NHAI, committees  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes NaBFID?
o: It was created in 2006 as an NBFC-IFC with paid-up capital of ₹5,000 crore.
It was created under SEBI regulations, 2014, to pool operating infrastructure.
It was created in 2015 as a Category II AIF manager with a ₹20,000 crore grant.
It was created under the NaBFID Act, 2021, with paid-up capital of ₹20,000 crore and a ₹5,000 crore grant.
accepted.x: NaBFID was established under the NaBFID Act, 2021, with ₹20,000 crore paid-up capital and a ₹5,000 crore grant.
accepted.tq: Use the founding law and capital structure to separate NaBFID from other financing institutions.
accepted.sec: Infrastructure financing and PPP - NIIF, NaBFID, IIFCL, InvITs, NHAI, committees  [other exams]

accepted.s: NaBFID had sanctioned approximately what amount by March 2025?
accepted.x: NaBFID had sanctioned ₹2,03,029 crore by March 2025.
accepted.tq: Distinguish sanctioned lending from paid-up capital and other infrastructure finance figures.
accepted.sec: Infrastructure financing and PPP - NIIF, NaBFID, IIFCL, InvITs, NHAI, committees  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: IIFCL — established in 2006 for long-term PPP finance; NBFC-IFC since 2013
IIFCL — established in 2015 as a quasi-sovereign wealth fund
IIFCL — established in 2014 under SEBI InvIT regulations
IIFCL — established in 2021 under the NaBFID Act
accepted.x: IIFCL was established in 2006 to provide long-term PPP finance and became an NBFC-IFC in 2013.
accepted.tq: Match the institution with both its founding year and regulatory status.
accepted.sec: Infrastructure financing and PPP - NIIF, NaBFID, IIFCL, InvITs, NHAI, committees  [other exams]

accepted.s: Infrastructure Investment Trusts, or InvITs, are governed by SEBI regulations of 2014 and are intended to:
accepted.x: InvITs are regulated under SEBI regulations of 2014 and pool operating infrastructure assets for investment and monetisation.
accepted.tq: Identify the instrument by its regulatory basis and functional purpose.
accepted.sec: Infrastructure financing and PPP - NIIF, NaBFID, IIFCL, InvITs, NHAI, committees  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT listed as a source or instrument of NHAI funding?
accepted.x: NHAI funding includes budget support, tolls, Toll-Operate-Transfer and InvITs. Agricultural income tax receipts are not listed as an NHAI funding source.
accepted.tq: Find the unrelated revenue source among the stated infrastructure financing mechanisms.
accepted.sec: Infrastructure financing and PPP - NIIF, NaBFID, IIFCL, InvITs, NHAI, committees  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly represents the NHAI monetisation and PPP pipeline figures?
o: ₹8.3 lakh crore monetised and a 1,520 km PPP pipeline worth ₹13,400 crore
₹2.03 lakh crore monetised and a 13,400 km PPP pipeline worth ₹5.8 lakh crore
₹1.52 lakh crore monetised and a 13,400 km PPP pipeline worth ₹8.3 lakh crore
₹1.52 lakh crore monetised and a 2,741 km PPP pipeline worth ₹11.17 lakh crore
accepted.x: NHAI had monetised ₹1.52 lakh crore, while its PPP pipeline covered 13,400 km and was valued at ₹8.3 lakh crore.
accepted.tq: Keep the monetised amount, route length and pipeline value in their correct order.
accepted.sec: Infrastructure financing and PPP - NIIF, NaBFID, IIFCL, InvITs, NHAI, committees  [other exams]

accepted.s: The Kelkar Committee of 2015 was associated with:
o: Revisiting and revitalising the PPP model
Setting up the National Monetisation Pipeline
accepted.x: The Kelkar Committee examined ways to revisit and revitalise the public-private partnership model.
accepted.tq: Match the committee with its specific policy mandate.
accepted.sec: Infrastructure financing and PPP - NIIF, NaBFID, IIFCL, InvITs, NHAI, committees  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which statement correctly reflects the change in the Centre's capital expenditure?
o: It remained fixed at ₹12.2 lakh crore from FY22 onwards.
It declined from ₹11.21 lakh crore in FY22 to ₹5.92 lakh crore in FY26.
It increased from ₹5.92 lakh crore in FY22 to ₹11.21 lakh crore in FY26; ₹12.2 lakh crore was provided in Budget 2026-27.
It increased from ₹5.8 lakh crore in FY22 to ₹16.72 lakh crore in FY26.
accepted.x: Central capital expenditure rose from ₹5.92 lakh crore in FY22 to ₹11.21 lakh crore in FY26, with ₹12.2 lakh crore provided in Budget 2026-27.
accepted.tq: Track the time sequence and distinguish annual expenditure from pipeline values.
accepted.sec: Infrastructure financing and PPP - NIIF, NaBFID, IIFCL, InvITs, NHAI, committees  [other exams]

accepted.s: The estimated multiplier associated with infrastructure capital expenditure is:
accepted.x: The infrastructure capital expenditure multiplier is estimated at approximately 2.5–3.5.
accepted.tq: Select the stated range rather than confusing it with an expenditure amount.
accepted.sec: Infrastructure financing and PPP - NIIF, NaBFID, IIFCL, InvITs, NHAI, committees  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which airport was the first airport in India built by a public limited company under the PPP model?
accepted.x: Cochin International Airport, established in 1999, was the first airport built by a public limited company under PPP.
accepted.tq: Identify the airport by combining its pioneering status, year and ownership model.
accepted.sec: Airports and ports - first company-owned airport, new airports, transhipment ports  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the growth in the number of operational airports?
accepted.x: The number of operational airports increased from 74 in 2014 to 164 in 2025.
accepted.tq: Preserve the chronological direction of the numerical comparison.
accepted.sec: Airports and ports - first company-owned airport, new airports, transhipment ports  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding greenfield airports:
1. Twenty-four greenfield airports have been approved.
2. Thirteen of them are operational.
3. Navi Mumbai is included among the operational airports.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Twenty-four greenfield airports have been approved, thirteen are operational, and Navi Mumbai is among the operational airports.
accepted.tq: Test the total, operational subset and named example together.
accepted.sec: Airports and ports - first company-owned airport, new airports, transhipment ports  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which of the following statements about Vizhinjam is correct?
o: It is India's first greenfield airport and was inaugurated in May 2025.
It is India's first inland waterway terminal and was inaugurated in 2021.
It is a railway freight corridor terminal inaugurated in 2025.
It is India's first deep-water transhipment port and first semi-automated container port.
accepted.x: Vizhinjam in Kerala is India's first deep-water transhipment port and first semi-automated container port; it was inaugurated in May 2025.
accepted.tq: Separate the port's two pioneering features from unrelated transport infrastructure.
accepted.sec: Airports and ports - first company-owned airport, new airports, transhipment ports  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with its status?
o: Vizhinjam — designated a customs port; Vadhvan and Great Nicobar — planned transhipment ports
Vizhinjam — planned; Vadhvan — operational customs port; Great Nicobar — airport
Vadhvan — first semi-automated container port; Vizhinjam — planned
Great Nicobar — operational airport; Vizhinjam — railway station
accepted.x: Vizhinjam was designated a customs port, while Vadhvan in Maharashtra and Great Nicobar were planned as further transhipment port projects.
accepted.tq: Separate the operational, designated and planned statuses of the three port locations.
accepted.sec: Airports and ports - first company-owned airport, new airports, transhipment ports  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which sequence correctly describes the milestones of Bhogapuram Airport?
o: Commercial operations on 17 August 2026, after PM inauguration on 1 August 2026; it replaces the INS Dega civil enclave.
PM inauguration on 17 August 2026, followed by commercial operations on 1 August 2026; it replaces Vizhinjam port.
PM inauguration on 1 June 2026, followed by commercial operations on 13 July 2026; it replaces Cochin Airport.
Commercial operations on 1 August 2026, after PM inauguration on 17 August 2026; it replaces Navi Mumbai Airport.
accepted.x: Bhogapuram, named Alluri Sitarama Raju International Airport, was inaugurated by the Prime Minister on 1 August 2026, began commercial operations on 17 August 2026 and replaces the INS Dega civil enclave.
accepted.tq: Use the first-and-second event sequence to eliminate reversed dates.
accepted.sec: Airports and ports - first company-owned airport, new airports, transhipment ports  [other exams]
